answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can charge a refundable stake locked for the life of an identity, like a lotus that only opens once its roots take hold: each new agent must escrow value it forfeits if it misbehaves, so spinning up a thousand fake identities costs a thousand stakes. Pair that with slow, peer-vouched onboarding — no agent becomes a full citizen overnight; it must earn trust over time, the way an island forms grain by grain and a dune holds only because every grain is anchored. The attacker then faces a real bill, not a free copy.
